boardProfile.layout: Block Out Level 47 has a unique staircase-shaped board where the left side descends in steps and the right side is a straight wall. Numbered counters `11`, `13`, `9`, and `22` are embedded in the staircase. The summit is misleading — the board opens from the right-side lane and the middle of the slope. Clear the `9` at the bottom-left first, peel the middle layers, and save the `22` at the bottom-right for last.
landmarks: Block Out Level 47 has a unique staircase-shaped board where the left side descends in steps and the right side is a straight wall.
Numbered counters `11`, `13`, `9`, and `22` are embedded in the staircase.
The summit is misleading — the board opens from the right-side lane and the middle of the slope.
Clear the `9` at the bottom-left first, peel the middle layers, and save the `22` at the bottom-right for last.

quickTips: The summit is a distraction — Level 47 opens from the right-side lane and the middle of the slope.
The `22` at the bottom-right is the last piece. Do not touch it until the middle layers are gone.
Think in chain clears. The best move is the one that sets up the next two moves, not just the quickest current match.

steps.title: Move 1
steps.instruction: Clear the `9` counter at the bottom-left to create the first opening.

steps.title: Move 2
steps.instruction: Open the right gadget lane and lower its counts.

steps.title: Move 3
steps.instruction: Peel the staircase from the middle — the `11` and `13` blocks — rather than the peak.

steps.title: Move 4
steps.instruction: Keep the upper tip of the staircase parked until the lower section is clear.

steps.title: Move 5
steps.instruction: Rotate the lower colored pieces through the opened pockets.

steps.title: Move 6
steps.instruction: Reduce the `22` counter at the bottom-right only after the middle is mostly gone.

steps.title: Move 7
steps.instruction: Finish with the upper staircase tip and the last side cleanup.

failurePoints: Starting at the very top of the staircase, which keeps the lower lanes clogged and wastes the only useful route.
Trying to reduce the `22` counter before the middle layers (`11` and `13`) are gone, which leaves no room for the heavy piece to move.
